summary.headline: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 133.9% to INR201.4 crore (26.1% margin) even as sales volume fell 26% to 38.9 KT.
summary.overview:
Standalone total income grew 6.6% to INR770.5 crore and PAT rose 150.3% to INR137.3 crore, driven by a sharp margin jump, while volumes dropped 26% as non-OEM buyers held back amid Middle East-driven raw material price volatility. Consolidated (India plus Thailand) volume was 50.8 KT, EBITDA INR223.6 crore at 22% margin. Management described the margin gain as a snapshot of a volatile quarter, not a sustainable run rate, and gave no volume guidance. The ABS capacity expansion is said to be on track for completion in FY27 without a firm commissioning month, and Thailand volumes remain subdued.</overview>

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Demand fell in the quarter, with a smaller drop than polystyrene; OEM is about 70% or more of ABS sales. Management did not give a segment volume split.

segments.name: Polystyrene (India)
segments.commentary: Hit harder than ABS, mainly in the non-OEM/unorganised segment; OEM is about 50% of PS sales. Management did not give volume numbers.

segments.name: SAN
segments.commentary: Merchant sales run at about 15,000-20,000 tonnes a year against roughly 100,000 tonnes of capacity; most output is used captively, and merchant sales will continue after the ABS expansion.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Running at low utilisation on specific products; volumes were broadly maintained quarter on quarter, but new business has not yet translated into meaningful volume growth. Validation cycles run 12-24 months.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance given; management said it is 'virtually impossible' to forecast given the current environment.
Management said Q1 margins are not indicative of sustainable performance; for modelling, assume margins similar to the existing business, with the expansion adding volume.
ABS expansion (about 50,000 tonnes in the chemical plant) to be completed in FY27; exact commissioning month not given.
Thailand: management expects volumes to improve over about three years, and margins to be much stronger once volumes arrive.
No new capex or capital allocation changes beyond the ABS expansion; polystyrene expansion to be decided when the business case is clearer.
capex_capacity: ABS expansion is a brownfield project at a running site, so commissioning is complex; management expects completion within FY27.
SAN capacity of about 100,000 tonnes against merchant sales of 15-20 KT a year; expansions planned across rubber, SAN and compounding sites.
Thailand cost base is described as higher than India's; no reduction timeline was given.
demand_pricing: Demand fell in Q1 due to a Middle East-driven price spike from March and high volatility; buyers in the non-OEM/unorganised segment held back. Management put the volume decline at about 15-25% on total polymer.

Styrene monomer went from about $1,000/t pre-war to $1,600-1,700, then about $1,200, and has since traded in a $1,100-1,400 range. Acrylonitrile moved from $1,200 to about $1,800-1,900 and is now $1,400-1,600. Butadiene (bought locally) went from $1,000 to above $2,500 and has since eased.
Styrene monomer is now sourced from alternate suppliers with 10-15 days longer lead times; management said it is 'fully covered' and carried slightly higher raw material inventory at quarter end.
Price pass-through is handled through short-term mechanisms and global price markers; management said previous-quarter pricing was significantly higher and moderated toward quarter end.
Imports: management said it has seen no significant change in import volumes, with some Asian exporters constrained by energy and naphtha shortages. Official import data is not available.

qa_highlights.question: How much did demand fall in India for ABS and PS, and was it driven by non-OEM buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the volume decline was in line across ABS and PS, roughly 15-25% on total polymer. The non-OEM segment was hit harder than OEM, which was affected only muted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin once the Q1 benefit reverses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was a snapshot of an unusual event and is not indicative of sustainable earnings; pre-event performance is the right base. It did not give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Will SAN merchant sales stop after ABS expansion, and what is the capex timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: SAN merchant sales will continue. The ABS expansion will be completed in FY27, but exact timing was not disclosed because the project runs alongside an operating plant.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any new capital allocation plan given extra cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new plan; cash will go to planned capex with the rest returned to shareholders in line with existing policy. No specific dividend or buyback was announced.

qa_highlights.question: What are Thailand's volume and sales plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Thailand sales strategy is to win validations in China, Japan, Vietnam, Korea and others; validations take 12-24 months. No volume guidance was given.

risks_watch: Sustainability of Q1 margins once the price gap and volatility normalise; the company declined to give a normalised margin figure.
Recovery of non-OEM volumes and whether destocking or channel stock effects reverse in the next nine months.
ABS expansion timing (within FY27) and execution risk on a brownfield site.
Thailand utilisation and validation progress; cost base still above India's.
Raw material lead times and alternate sourcing for styrene monomer and acrylonitrile; freight and energy disruptions.
Limited import data availability, which makes competitive import pressure hard to track.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategy and balance sheet, but guarded on numbers: management declined to give volume guidance, timeline precision, margin normalisation or current-quarter pricing, citing volatility.
